answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because lagoon only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, dune is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any walnut approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
